text:
Priya: forwarding customer report — they upgraded to a paid plan but immediately started seeing 401s and 429s; they cant get past the quota. pasted their note below.

Priya: --- customer pasted ---
Customer: after upgrading, some requests succeed but a lot return 429 (quota exceeded) or 401 (invalid token). happening across regions. using our hosted API via SDK. timestamps and request ids attached.

Alex: thanks — can you share account id + a couple of request_ids + exact time window? Also did they change API key or rotate tokens during upgrade?

Priya: account: acct_98765. request_ids: req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789. window: 2026-11-02T14:12:00Z -> 14:22:00Z. customer says they clicked "Upgrade to Pro" in console around 14:05 and card shows charged.

Alex: ok. common pattern: billing/plan change didn't fully propagate to quota service or payment gateway failed and UI showed upgraded state incorrectly. sharing what Im seeing from logs for req_abc123:
```json
{"timestamp":"2026-11-02T14:13:02Z","request_id":"req_abc123","status":429,"error":"quota_exceeded","plan_shard":"free-tier"}
```

Priya: customer also shared curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello world"}'
```

Shreya: I looked up acct_98765 — payment attempted but declined by card issuer (AVS mismatch). invoice inv_20261102_987 not fully cleared. The console shows upgrade requested but the billing state is still "pending_payment" so quota service kept free-tier limits. I can attach the decline reason to the case and email the customer.

Marcos: from sales: we can approve a short temporary quota lift while billing works with the customer, but need approvals for any >2h increase. what's the requested capacity?

Priya: customer needs a short burst window to finish a demo — roughly 200 concurrent requests / 5k tokens/min for 2-4 hours. They asked if we can "flip a switch" now.

Alex: mitigation while we sort billing: 1) add server-side 429 retry with exponential backoff and jitter 2) reduce parallel clients and use longer session/keep-alive 3) enable KV/prefix caching if applicable. sample retry pattern: 
```python
import time
for attempt in range(5):
    resp = client.call(...)
    if resp.status != 429:
        break
    sleep = (2 ** attempt) * 0.5 + random.random() * 0.1
    time.sleep(sleep)
```

Priya: submitting a temporary quota lift request to operations. tagging @quota-bot to automate. :eyes:

quota-bot: quota lift request created for acct_98765: request_id=qreq_20261102_01, requested_limit=500r/s, ttl=4h, status=pending_approval

Marcos: approved. set TTL to 3 hours for now. I'll own the follow-up and confirm if they want a full commit.

quota-bot: approved by Marcos; applying temporary quota: new_limit=500r/s, expires_at=2026-11-02T17:15:00Z. change applied to edge routing and quota service.

Priya: replied to customer: temporary lift applied for 3 hours while billing investigates. suggested retry/backoff + lower concurrency as immediate mitigation. asking them to confirm traffic looks normal.

Shreya: billing will email customer with next steps to clear payment and finish upgrade. once payment clears well remove the temporary flag and promote them to paid quota. Ill attach invoice and next-billing steps to the ticket.

Alex: logging note: correlate future 429s with plan_shard and billing_state to avoid false positives; we should add an alert if plan_shard != billing_state for any account. filing a small infra ticket to detect this.

Priya: closing loop for now — customer confirmed they can proceed with demo and will update after billing. tagging for handoff: @Marcos (sales) to close upgrade sale; @Shreya (billing) to clear invoice. :thumbsup:
